verses.1: And the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, “In the land of Egypt, say this.”
verses.2: This new year is the beginning of new things for you. It’s a time for you to start anew in the new year.
verses.3: They spoke to all the tribes of Israel, saying, “On the twentieth day of this month, they shall take a male servant for each household.”
verses.4: And if the house becomes unclean, then he shall take it away and bring its neighbors to his house. Each person shall be punished according to their own actions.
verses.5: Let there be a pure, innocent boy of one year old. You shall take him from among the livestock and from among the wild animals.
verses.6: And it shall be for you to keep this month for forty days. On that day, every man from the people of Israel must slaughter an animal.
verses.7: And they took some of the blood, and applied it to the two doors, as well as to the doorposts in the houses where people ate it.
verses.8: And they ate the meat during this night, under the shade of the trees. They ate it with spices on top of it.
verses.9: Do not eat from it, please. Do not drink from its water either. Its head must be covered with fire, along with its body.
verses.10: And they shall not be allowed to leave it until morning. And those who try to leave it before morning will be destroyed by fire.
verses.11: And in this way, you will eat it. Your leaders will hold you down with their hands and feet, and you will eat it hastily. This is what the Lord has commanded.
verses.12: And I passed through the land of Egypt at this night. I destroyed every animal and man in the land of Egypt. And for all the gods of Egypt, I will carry out judgments. I am Jehovah.
verses.13: And the blood shall be a sign for you on the doors of those houses where you are. I saw the blood, and I abhorred you. There will be no more sin in your hearts when I strike the land of Egypt.
verses.14: And this day shall be for you a reminder and a celebration of it. It shall be a feast for Jehovah, a covenant of everlastingness for your generations.
verses.15: For seven days, you shall eat this food. But on the first day, you must sacrifice all the remaining animals from your herd. For every animal that is eaten during these seven days, that person will be considered unclean. This rule applies to everyone in Israel, from the beginning until the seventh day.
verses.16: And on the first day, it is a sacred day; and on the seventh day, it is also a sacred day. On those days, no work shall be done at all. But whatever is eaten by everyone shall be for your own use alone.
verses.17: And you shall keep these laws, for today, in this very day, I have brought your tribes out of the land of Egypt. And you shall keep this day as a foreverlasting law for your descendants.
verses.18: On the first day of the twelfth day of the month, in the afternoon, they will eat matzot until the day of Erev. And on the twentieth day of the month, again in the afternoon.
verses.19: For seven days, no one in your tribe will be able to find anything to eat. For all food becomes bitter and tasteless; that soul is destroyed from among the Israelites, both in the wilderness and on the land.
verses.20: Do not eat any roasted meat in all your seats. Instead, eat vegetables instead.
verses.21: And Moses called out to all the elders of Israel. He said to them, “Go and take some sheep for your families. Slaughter them during the Passover festival.”
verses.22: And you took Agedot from Ezov, and you immersed it in the blood that was in the vessel. Then you brought it to the altar, along with the two vessels made of blood. And no one was allowed to leave the house’s door until evening came.
verses.23: And Jehovah passed by the gates of Egypt. He saw the blood on the doors and on the two pillars. Then Jehovah sealed the gates, so that no one could enter your city.
verses.24: And you shall keep this commandment as a law for yourself and for your descendants forever.
verses.25: And it shall be, when you enter the land that Jehovah gives to you, as he has spoken, and as you have kept this commandment.
verses.26: And it will be like when they say to you, “What is this labor that you are doing?”
verses.27: And you said, “This is a sacrifice for the Lord. It was offered by the children of Israel in Egypt. He destroyed Egypt and saved our people. He honored them.”
verses.28: And the children of Israel did as Jehovah commanded Moses and Aaron. They did just as He said.
verses.29: And it happened at midnight, and God destroyed every tomb in the land of Egypt. From the tomb of Pharaoh who sat on his throne, all the way down to the tombs of the slaves who were in the prison. Every tomb was destroyed.
verses.30: And Pharaoh, along with all his servants and all the Egyptians, stood up in a great cry of despair. For there was no one alive in the house at all.
verses.31: And he called Moses and Aaron in the night. He said, “Come out! Let us go out from among my people. Also, let the Israelites also go out. And let them serve the LORD, as you have been commanded.”
verses.32: And also, when you go out and about, do as you have said. And then go away from there. And may God bless you too.
verses.33: And Egypt became stronger over the people, and they were forced to be sent away from the land. For they said, “We are all dead.”
verses.34: And the people took their clothes off before they were angry with their remains, with their clothes still on their bodies.
verses.35: And the children of Israel did as Moses commanded them. They brought back from Egypt all kinds of gold and silver jewelry, as well as clothes.
verses.36: And Jehovah showed the kindness of His people to the Egyptians. He saved them from their enemies.
verses.37: And the sons of Israel traveled from Reamsess Sukhotah, about six miles away from the giants alone.
verses.38: And also, in the evening, there was plenty of food for them, along with sheep and other provisions. In the morning, they had delicious food to eat.
verses.39: They burned the pots that they took out of Egypt. They burned them because they didn’t want to use them anymore after being taken out of Egypt. They couldn’t even use them for any other purpose either.
verses.40: And those who lived in Egypt, among the Israelites, remained there for thirty years and four months.
verses.41: And it was three hundred years and four thousand days ago. And on this very day, all of God’s people came out of Egypt.
verses.42: The night of Shmini-Rimmon is a night for Jehovah to bring them out of the land of Egypt. This is the night that Jehovah sets aside for all the children of Israel, as a time of celebration.
verses.43: And the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, “This is the law for Passover: No kind of bird shall eat anything that belongs to Passover.”
verses.44: And every servant who is bought with money will eat from it.
verses.45: A person who is hired or employed – does not eat from it.
verses.46: In one house, nothing shall be eaten that is not taken from the house. Neither meat nor any other food shall be left in it.
verses.47: All of Israel will do it.
verses.48: And if a worm dwells in you, and he makes sacrifices to the LORD, then every living creature will bring its offerings. Then it will be like the earth itself; no one will be able to eat from it.
verses.49: One Torah will be given to the common people and to the poor among them.
verses.50: And all the children of Israel did as Jehovah commanded Moses and Aaron. They did so accordingly.
verses.51: And on this very day, Jehovah brought out the children of Israel from Egypt, onto their feet.
